title: Compact Pool Operations Lens — Burst & Autoscale Controls Prototype
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a compact, high-density operations lens for Redwood Console focused on Dedicated GPU pools. The lens surfaces key health signals, an actionable burst dial, and an autoscale composer that prioritizes SLO-safe scaling decisions and shows cost impact previews. Target users: SREs, platform engineers, and capacity ops. Deliverables: interactive Figma prototype (desktop/tablet), annotated handoff spec, usability findings. Goals: reduce mean time to remediation for pool incidents, make burst configuration discoverable and safe, and provide transparent cost/latency tradeoff guidance.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype shows a single-row compact pool card that expands to a detail sheet with: real-time health sparkline, slot utilization, estimated queue depth, and recent failover events
Burst dial UI allows preset quick-burst (1m, 5m, 15m) and custom burst sizing with preview of reserved vs borrowed capacity and estimated token cost delta
Autoscale composer suggests 3 profiles (conservative, balanced, aggressive) with projected 24h cost and 99th latency estimate; user can edit, simulate, and commit to rollout
All interactive states documented in Figma with accessibility color tokens and keyboard flows
Developer handoff includes a telemetry contract (metric names + sampling) and frontend animations spec
Design review sign-off from PM and Eng with at least two actionable engineering follow-ups
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff with PM and Eng. Agreed scope: single compact lens + expandable detail sheet. Telemetry constraint: 2s resolution for critical metrics.
2026-02-20: Initial wireframes v0.1 created. Focus on micro-interactions for burst dial and simulated cost widget.
2026-02-28: Usability test with 6 platform engineers. Key insight: users want instant rollback on burst and clearer signal of 'borrowed' GPU usage vs reserved capacity.
2026-03-02: Iterated prototype to surface a 'safety envelope' indicator and inline rollback button. Added autoscale profiles and cost-preview modal.
2026-03-05: Design doc & prototype submitted for engineering review. Awaiting perf feasibility answers about KV-cache telemetry and batch-level metrics availability.
review_feedback: PM (Samir Torres): Prefer conservative defaults tied to customer tier; avoid auto-commit on aggressive profiles without explicit confirmation.
Eng (Priya Nambiar): Burst implementation feasible but needs server-side quota check; propose adding a 'preflight quota check' step before commit.
SRE (Carlos Ruiz): Suggest a 'simulated load' toggle that approximates impact on latency under current telemetry sampling — can be approximated client-side for preview.
Design critique (Leah Armstrong): Information density is high on expanded sheet; recommend progressive disclosure and microcopy for cost estimates.
next_steps: Engineering feasibility sync (Priya) to confirm metric shapes and quota preflight API by 2026-03-10
Add accessibility test cases and update color tokens for color-blind contrast
Split handoff into two ENG tickets: frontend (compact lens + detail sheet) and backend (quota check + cost estimator endpoint)
Schedule design pairing session during Cycle 2026-W06 for micro-interaction polish
